claims.claim: Elizabeth Bear calls Hobb generally a fine stylist in very good control of her writing.
claims.source: Elizabeth Bear, Tor.com review of Dragon Keeper, 2010
claims.quote: in very good control of her writing, and a fine stylist
claims.routeHint: wayback raw capture 20221003055909id_ of the tor.com URL; reactormag.com returns 403

claims.claim: Bear judges the prose of Dragon Keeper rougher than she expects of Hobb.
claims.source: Elizabeth Bear, Tor.com review of Dragon Keeper, 2010
claims.quote: the prose felt rougher than I expect of Hobb

claims.claim: Bear calls the interpolated dispatches between two pigeon-keepers a great expositional trick.
claims.source: Elizabeth Bear, Tor.com review of Dragon Keeper, 2010
claims.quote: It’s a great expositional trick

claims.claim: Bear reports caring deeply about the pigeon-keepers' negotiations over squabs, apprentices and bags of feed.
claims.source: Elizabeth Bear, Tor.com review of Dragon Keeper, 2010
claims.quote: negotiations over squabs, apprentices, and bags of feed

claims.claim: Bear calls the carrier-pigeon keepers' scribbled messages one of the more enchanting aspects of Dragon Haven.
claims.source: Elizabeth Bear, Tor.com review of Dragon Haven, 2010
claims.quote: whose scribbled messages to one another remain one of the more enchanting aspects

claims.claim: Hobb says her writing has evolved by slowing down and putting in the small details.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Peter Orullian, Tor.com, 2012
claims.quote: I slow down and put in the small details
claims.page: answer to 'How has your own writing evolved'

claims.claim: Hobb says every story starts with a character who then introduces the setting, culture, conflict, government and economy.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Peter Orullian, Tor.com, 2012
claims.quote: introduces setting, culture, conflict, government, economy

claims.claim: Hobb names as her favourite books those where a protagonist takes part in great events that also strongly affect the little lives.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Peter Orullian, Tor.com, 2012
claims.quote: participate in great events that also impact the little lives very strongly
claims.page: answer to 'What makes a fantasy epic?'

claims.claim: Hobb says the familiar element is what invites the reader in and makes a strange story real.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Peter Orullian, Tor.com, 2012
claims.quote: the familiar is what invites the reader in and makes it real
claims.page: answer on blending strange and familiar

claims.claim: Hobb says that when writing from a character's point of view the author must stop making judgments and let the character talk.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Peter Orullian, Tor.com, 2012
claims.quote: the author has to stop making judgments and let the character talk
claims.page: answer on how her writing has evolved

claims.claim: Hobb says something about the Robin Hobb style does not lend itself to tales shorter than a novella.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, '5000 Words About Myself', 2004
claims.quote: Something about the style does not lend itself to shorter tales
claims.routeHint: wayback raw capture 20050724083052id_; the live robinhobb.com URL now returns 404

claims.claim: Hobb says the way to convince a reader she knows dragons is to know the details of raising chickens or roofing a house.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, '5000 Words About Myself', 2004
claims.quote: the details of raising chickens or putting a roof on a house

claims.claim: Hobb says she tries to experience what she writes about so as to include its physical details in the stories.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, '5000 Words About Myself', 2004
claims.quote: include the physical details of them in the stories

claims.claim: Hobb says she began the first Farseer book intending a completely different sort of voice and telling.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, '5000 Words About Myself', 2004
claims.quote: to attempt a completely different sort of voice and telling
claims.page: paragraph on choosing the Robin Hobb by-line

claims.claim: Natasha Pulley notes that Hobb declines to name the garden maid outright, which would have been the narratively efficient move.
claims.source: Natasha Pulley, 'Character is in the Details: Robin Hobb's Golden Fool', Tor.com, 2015
claims.quote: which would have been the narratively efficient thing to do
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'There's an unobtrusive moment'

claims.claim: Pulley reads Fitz's insistence on the colour of straw as carrying his stable upbringing against the Fool's courtly one.
claims.source: Natasha Pulley, 'Character is in the Details: Robin Hobb's Golden Fool', Tor.com, 2015
claims.quote: What’s brilliant, though, is that he does it over straw
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'That Fitz goes straight'

claims.claim: Pulley says the Tawny Man trilogy has pin-sharp moments alongside its dragons and sweeping landscapes.
claims.source: Natasha Pulley, 'Character is in the Details: Robin Hobb's Golden Fool', Tor.com, 2015
claims.quote: but it has these pin-sharp moments too

claims.claim: Stephanie Dray attributes to Hobb a grim devotion to realistic consequences in the Liveship Traders books.
claims.source: Stephanie Dray, Strange Horizons review of the Liveship Traders series, 2001
claims.quote: This grim devotion to realistic consequences

claims.claim: Dray writes that Hobb is not afraid to maim, disfigure or transform her characters.
claims.source: Stephanie Dray, Strange Horizons review of the Liveship Traders series, 2001
claims.quote: she isn’t afraid to maim, disfigure, or transform

claims.claim: Dray characterises all of Hobb's works as marked by a general glum realism.
claims.source: Stephanie Dray, Strange Horizons review of the Liveship Traders series, 2001
claims.quote: the general glum realism of all of her works
claims.page: body, paragraph on Ship of Destiny

claims.claim: Dray faults the series for occasionally jarring shifts in point of view.
claims.source: Stephanie Dray, Strange Horizons review of the Liveship Traders series, 2001
claims.quote: the occasionally jarring shifts in point of view

claims.claim: Ilana Teitelbaum says the emphasis at Withywoods is on what is textured, tangible and handmade.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, 'Bright Home, Dark Heart', Los Angeles Review of Books, 2014
claims.quote: the emphasis is on what is textured, tangible, handmade
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'While Hobb's generosity with detail'

claims.claim: Teitelbaum observes that conversation at Withywoods turns to the uses of herbs and the seasons for crops rather than battle or intrigue.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, 'Bright Home, Dark Heart', Los Angeles Review of Books, 2014
claims.quote: conversations turn to the uses of herbs, the seasons for crops
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'This is not only a contrast'

claims.claim: Teitelbaum notes that in Fool's Assassin writing tablets and books count as luxuries.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, 'Bright Home, Dark Heart', Los Angeles Review of Books, 2014
claims.quote: Writing tablets and books are luxuries
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'While Hobb's generosity with detail'

claims.claim: Teitelbaum says what is most important in Hobb's character development is what is not said.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, 'Bright Home, Dark Heart', Los Angeles Review of Books, 2014
claims.quote: what is most important is what is not said

claims.claim: Teitelbaum says Fitz's limited point of view leaves the world as enigmatic to him as to the reader.
claims.source: Ilana Teitelbaum, 'Bright Home, Dark Heart', Los Angeles Review of Books, 2014
claims.quote: Fitz’s limited point of view renders the world as enigmatic to him

claims.claim: Justin Landon says Fool's Assassin is, without question, a slow novel.
claims.source: Justin Landon, Tor.com review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: It is, without question, a slow novel

claims.claim: Landon says Fool's Assassin is better compared to pastoral family dramas than to action-packed epic fantasies.
claims.source: Justin Landon, Tor.com review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: Comparing it to more pastoral family dramas would be more appropriate

claims.claim: Landon says the journal entries opening every chapter are how Hobb reminds the reader of what has come before.
claims.source: Justin Landon, Tor.com review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: These entries, which open every chapter
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Fool's Assassin returns to the inside'

claims.claim: Landon describes Fitz as reliably unreliably interpreting the actions of those around him.
claims.source: Justin Landon, Tor.com review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: reliably unreliably interpreting the actions of those around him
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Fool's Assassin returns to the inside'

claims.claim: Jane Shilling calls the elegant translucence of Hobb's prose deceptive.
claims.source: Jane Shilling, The Daily Telegraph review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: the elegant translucence of her prose is deceptive
claims.routeHint: wayback raw capture 20250725002840id_; live telegraph.co.uk is paywalled

claims.claim: Shilling says Hobb is interested not in fine writing but in writing that offers the least resistance between reader and story.
claims.source: Jane Shilling, The Daily Telegraph review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: writing that offers the least resistance between reader and story

claims.claim: Shilling summarises the Six Duchies in institutional terms: states skirmishing, aristocratic intrigues festering, farmers threatened by sea raiders.
claims.source: Jane Shilling, The Daily Telegraph review of Fool's Assassin, 2014
claims.quote: states skirmish, aristocratic intrigues fester, and farmers are threatened

claims.claim: Matthew Oliver describes the chapter epigraphs of Assassin's Apprentice as a formal history written in a distant, scholarly voice.

claims.quote: a distant, scholarly voice

claims.claim: Oliver says the novel's first epigraph opens with the authoritative voice of History establishing a clear centre to its narrative.
claims.source: Matthew Oliver, Mythlore 41.1 (Fall/Winter 2022), 'History in the Margins'
claims.quote: the authoritative voice of History establishing a clear center
claims.page: p. 53, section 'Historical Authority in Assassin's Apprentice'

claims.claim: Oliver observes that the epigraph describing Patience cites evidentiary quotes from her nursemaids instead of the narrator's own acquaintance with her.
claims.source: Matthew Oliver, Mythlore 41.1 (Fall/Winter 2022), 'History in the Margins'
claims.quote: he includes evidentiary quotes from her
claims.page: p. 56, discussion of the Chapter 13 epigraph

claims.claim: Oliver calls the history that opens each chapter dry and impersonal beside the personal main text.
claims.source: Matthew Oliver, Mythlore 41.1 (Fall/Winter 2022), 'History in the Margins'
claims.quote: the dry, impersonal, but
claims.page: p. 57, end of the Patience discussion
claims.confidence: medium — the quoted phrase runs across a line break in the PDF text layer

claims.claim: Oliver names Hobb's most striking stylistic device negative narration: describing what is not happening before what is.
claims.source: Matthew Oliver, Mythlore 41.1 (Fall/Winter 2022), 'History in the Margins'
claims.quote: double negatives (of which there are many)

claims.claim: Oliver reports that in the early chapters of Assassin's Apprentice scarcely a page goes by without an example of negative construction.
claims.source: Matthew Oliver, Mythlore 41.1 (Fall/Winter 2022), 'History in the Margins'
claims.quote: scarcely a page goes by without obvious examples

claims.claim: Oliver identifies extensive parataxis, elevated figurative language and parallelism as the elevated fantasy style Fitz shifts into when he narrates an invented vision.
claims.source: Matthew Oliver, Mythlore 41.1 (Fall/Winter 2022), 'History in the Margins'
claims.quote: elevated figurative language, and parallelism
claims.page: pp. 59-60, section on the duchess's vision

claims.claim: Oliver frames the novel's structure as a discursive conflict between public and private, official history and personal myth-making.
claims.source: Matthew Oliver, Mythlore 41.1 (Fall/Winter 2022), 'History in the Margins'
claims.quote: public vs. private, official history vs. personal myth
